moduleTitle: Module 3. Sensory, Motor, Autonomic and Endocrine Physiology

competencies.name: Sensory transduction
competencies.can: Explain how a stimulus is converted into a receptor potential and how that graded potential becomes a train of action potentials in the sensory neuron.

competencies.name: Receptor classification
competencies.can: Classify a receptor by stimulus type as a mechanoreceptor, chemoreceptor, thermoreceptor, photoreceptor, or nociceptor and give a body location for each.

competencies.name: Stimulus coding
competencies.can: Explain how the nervous system encodes modality, location, intensity, and duration and identify the labeled line principle.

competencies.name: Receptive fields and acuity
competencies.can: Relate receptive field size and lateral inhibition to two point discrimination and predict which body regions have the finest acuity.

competencies.name: Receptor adaptation
competencies.can: Distinguish tonic from phasic receptors by their adaptation rate and match each to a stimulus the body needs to monitor continuously or only at onset.

competencies.name: Somatosensory pathways
competencies.can: Trace touch and pain information from receptor to cortex and explain why the somatosensory homunculus is disproportionate.

competencies.name: Pain and its modulation
competencies.can: Distinguish fast and slow pain by fiber type, explain referred pain by convergence, and describe how gate control and endogenous opioids reduce pain transmission.

competencies.name: Tactile mapping and adaptation testing
competencies.can: Measure two point discrimination at several body sites and show receptor adaptation and referred sensation experimentally.

competencies.name: Optics and accommodation
competencies.can: Explain refraction by the cornea and lens and describe how accommodation and the pupillary reflex focus near and far images.

competencies.name: Phototransduction
competencies.can: Trace phototransduction from photon absorption by retinal through the change in cyclic GMP to the decrease in glutamate release and explain why photoreceptors hyperpolarize to light.

competencies.name: Rods cones and visual processing
competencies.can: Compare rods and cones by sensitivity and acuity and trace the visual pathway to predict the field deficit produced by a lesion at the optic nerve or the optic chiasm.

competencies.name: Refractive errors and clinical vision
competencies.can: Explain myopia, hyperopia, presbyopia, and astigmatism in terms of focal point and eyeball or lens shape and state the corrective lens for each.

competencies.name: Auditory transduction
competencies.can: Trace sound from the tympanic membrane through the ossicles and cochlear fluid to hair cell bending and auditory nerve firing and explain how pitch and loudness are coded.

competencies.name: Conductive and sensorineural hearing loss
competencies.can: Distinguish conductive from sensorineural hearing loss by the site of the lesion and by the expected Weber and Rinne results.

competencies.name: Equilibrium
competencies.can: Explain how the semicircular canals detect angular acceleration and how the utricle and saccule detect linear acceleration and head position.

competencies.name: Taste and smell
competencies.can: Compare gustatory and olfactory transduction and explain why olfactory input reaches the limbic system without a thalamic relay.

competencies.name: Vision testing
competencies.can: Perform visual acuity, blind spot, accommodation, and color vision testing and interpret each result.

competencies.name: Hearing and equilibrium testing
competencies.can: Perform Weber and Rinne tuning fork tests and a balance test and interpret the findings.

competencies.name: Motor control hierarchy
competencies.can: Order the levels of motor control from spinal reflex through brainstem to cortex and state what each level contributes to a voluntary movement.

competencies.name: Corticospinal pathway
competencies.can: Trace the corticospinal pathway from the primary motor cortex to the skeletal muscle and identify where it crosses.

competencies.name: Cerebellum and basal ganglia
competencies.can: Contrast the contributions of the cerebellum and the basal ganglia to movement and match a described motor sign to the structure involved.

competencies.name: Upper and lower motor neuron signs
competencies.can: Distinguish upper from lower motor neuron lesions by tone, reflexes, and muscle bulk and assign a set of findings to the correct level.

competencies.name: Autonomic and somatic organization
competencies.can: Contrast the somatic motor system with the autonomic two neuron pathway by neuron count and by effector tissue.

competencies.name: Sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions
competencies.can: Compare the two autonomic divisions by CNS origin and ganglion location and predict the effect of each on heart rate and on the gastrointestinal tract.

competencies.name: Autonomic neurotransmitters and receptors
competencies.can: Match nicotinic, muscarinic, alpha, and beta receptors to their neurotransmitter, their location, and the response each produces.

competencies.name: Dual innervation and tonic control
competencies.can: Explain dual innervation and autonomic tone and predict the effect of removing one division from a dually innervated organ.

competencies.name: Adrenal medulla
competencies.can: Explain why the adrenal medulla is a modified sympathetic ganglion and compare the duration of its circulating catecholamine effect with direct sympathetic innervation.

competencies.name: Autonomic pharmacology
competencies.can: Predict the effect of a beta blocker or a muscarinic antagonist on a named organ from the receptor it targets.

competencies.name: Autonomic function testing
competencies.can: Measure heart rate variability and the response to a cold pressor or orthostatic challenge and interpret the result as sympathetic or parasympathetic dominance.

competencies.name: Hormone classes
competencies.can: Classify hormones as peptide, steroid, or amine and compare the three by synthesis, storage, and receptor location.

competencies.name: Hormone transport and half life
competencies.can: Explain how protein binding in plasma affects the free hormone fraction and the half life and predict which hormone class circulates bound.

competencies.name: Hormone receptors and target response
competencies.can: Explain why one hormone can produce different responses in different tissues and relate receptor number to target cell sensitivity.

competencies.name: Hormone interactions
competencies.can: Define synergism, permissiveness, and antagonism and identify each in a described hormone pair.

competencies.name: Control of hormone release
competencies.can: Classify a hormone stimulus as humoral, neural, or hormonal and trace an example of each.

competencies.name: Hypothalamic pituitary axes
competencies.can: Trace a three tier axis from hypothalamic releasing hormone through the anterior pituitary trophic hormone to the peripheral gland and place the long and short loop negative feedback.

competencies.name: Primary and secondary endocrine disorders
competencies.can: Use hormone levels at two tiers of an axis to classify a disorder as primary or secondary and as hypersecretion or hyposecretion.

competencies.name: Posterior pituitary hormones
competencies.can: Explain why the posterior pituitary is neural tissue and state the stimulus and target action of antidiuretic hormone and oxytocin.

competencies.name: Growth hormone
competencies.can: Describe the direct and insulin like growth factor mediated actions of growth hormone and predict the result of excess or deficiency before and after epiphyseal closure.

competencies.name: Thyroid hormone
competencies.can: Trace thyroid hormone synthesis, state the metabolic actions of T3 and T4, and match hyperthyroid and hypothyroid signs to the underlying rate of metabolism.

competencies.name: Adrenal cortex
competencies.can: Match the three cortical zones to aldosterone, cortisol, and the adrenal androgens and state the primary action of each.

competencies.name: Cortisol and the stress response
competencies.can: Describe the metabolic, immune, and cardiovascular actions of cortisol and explain the consequences of chronic elevation.

competencies.name: Calcium homeostasis
competencies.can: Trace the response to falling plasma calcium through parathyroid hormone, calcitriol, and the actions on bone, kidney, and intestine, and state the role of calcitonin.

competencies.name: Pancreatic islet hormones
competencies.can: Compare insulin and glucagon by stimulus and by effect on liver glycogen and on plasma glucose and identify the islet cell that secretes each.

competencies.name: Diabetes mellitus
competencies.can: Distinguish type 1 from type 2 diabetes by mechanism and explain how untreated hyperglycemia produces polyuria and ketoacidosis.

competencies.name: Glucose tolerance testing
competencies.can: Plot a glucose tolerance curve from measured or simulated data and distinguish a normal response from an impaired one.

competencies.name: Hormone assay
competencies.can: Run or simulate an immunoassay for a hormone and use the standard curve to determine an unknown concentration.
